ana: Heads-up — PM Evan pushed a customer ask (FarrowHealth) to prioritize a KV-cache policy change. They see huge token spend on 8k+ chats and want a viable launch plan for caching + kernel preference.
ev an (PM): Quick context: Farrow is hitting ~2x token cost on long sessions. Ask: prefix caching (session-level), deterministic keying so they can pin sensitive prefixes, and guidance to prefer lower-precision kernels where accuracy is acceptable. They want launch criteria they can share with security and procurement.
mike: TL;DR: doable but touches kernel selection, quantization paths, and cache eviction. Need to decide opt-in vs global. Also need rollout telemetry.
sofia: Important edge cases: multi-tenant cache poisoning, per-customer isolation, cache warm-up spikes, TTLs for context that contains PII.
jordan: For rollout — propose canary by customer + model variant. Metrics: p95 latency, cache_hit_rate, token_cost_per_session, KV_memory_bytes, cache_eviction_rate, and semantic regression (BLEU/ROUGE or eval prompts).
ana (typo fix) ana: (lol) noted.
ev an (PM): Customer constraint: security team requires that any cached prefix can be scoped to customer-owned KMS or have an explicit opt-in selector. They won’t accept a global default.
mike: Proposed scope negotiation: Phase 1 = opt-in runtime flag in model config + per-customer isolation; Phase 2 = auto-enabled with heuristic suggestions from Redwood Optimize after proven safe. That minimizes blast radius.
sofia: Implementation notes: keying should be deterministic across replicas: e.g., key = sha256(customer_id + model_id + prefix_hash). Avoid user-id only. Eviction policy: LRU with size and TTL caps, plus manual invalidation API.
sofia: code snippet for config:```
model_cache:
  enabled: true
  scope: customer
  keying: "sha256(customer_id||model_id||prefix_hash)"
  eviction: lru
  ttl_seconds: 86400
  max_bytes: 1073741824
```
mike: Kernel interplay: when cache hits return short-token generation we still need to pick kernels for next-token compute. Suggest: honor model quantization profile pinned by customer, but allow runtime fallback to higher-precision kernel on low-latency critical paths. Need acceptance criteria around correctness vs perf.
jordan: Acceptance criteria (draft, copyable into PRD):
- Feature gate: opt-in flag exist and defaults to off for existing customers.
- Isolation: cached entries scoped by customer_id and model_id (no cross-tenant hits).
- Safety: TTL + invalidation API + KMS integration for customers that opt for encrypted cache.
- Performance: for canary customers, p95 generation latency <= 200ms for steps that hit the cache, and overall token_cost_per_session reduces by >= 30% on average.
- Correctness: semantic regression score on eval prompt set does not degrade > 1% relative to baseline model for cached paths.
- Resource: KV memory usage per node stays under configured max and eviction works without OOM.
- Rollout: canary for 5 internal accounts, then 3 pilot customers, then broader opt-in.
sofia: Edge cases to add to acceptance criteria: long-prefix fragmentation (prefix > 64k), model version mismatch in cache (must include model_version in key), and quantized kernel desync (cache entries must record kernel profile used).
mike: For PRD scope negotiation: keep L0 simple (opt-in customer-scoped cache + LRU + TTL + invalidation API + metrics). L1 adds automatic heuristics + Optimize suggestions + global opt-in later.
ev an (PM): Customer ok with opt-in pilot next week if we can show telemetry + privacy docs. I'm adding legal & security to review.
infra-bot: CI note: new e2e will run cache correctness + eviction tests. Suggest we add perf microbench to infra pipeline for quantized kernels.
jordan: I will spin up the RFC/PRD and assign owners: eng-runtime (mike, sofia) and product (evan). Target PRD draft by Thu.
ana (again typo) ana: ack — I'll coordinate pilot comms with Farrow.
mike: Action items: 1) Mike & Sofia: sketch RFC with interfaces + metrics 2) Jordan: PRD shell + rollout plan 3) Evan: legal/security sync with Farrow 4) Ana: pilot comms and acceptance sign-off.
sofia: small note: we need a fallback policy when cache index corrupted — prefer safe fallback to cold-run instead of returning cached tokens. Add fallback test to acceptance.
nana ana: :eyes: noted.
ev an (PM): Thanks all — pushing timeline into roadmap now.
infra-bot: deploy-bot scheduled canary window: next_mon_03:00-07:00 UTC.
mike: ok, will post RFC link here when ready.
